Introduces SMOTE itself, a new oversampler that interpolates between a minority sample and one of its k minority nearest neighbours (Sec. 4.2, Algorithm SMOTE), so own; SMOTE plus under-sampling is compared with plain under-sampling and replication oversampling (Sec. 5, Figs. 4-5 and 7-23).

A modified back-propagation balances the training set with standard SMOTE and then sets, each epoch, how many minority samples to feed from a per-class MSE ratio (Sec. 2, Algorithm 1), a new rule for how much to oversample, so own; compared with standard SMOTE (Table 2).

OAA-DB applies the authors' earlier SMOTE-then-CMTNN-cleaning balancing unchanged to each one-against-all subproblem and adds a codeword decision rule (Sec. II.C-D), so existing-parts; the baselines are only OAA, OAO, A&O and OAHO, decomposition schemes (OAHO is called a balancing technique but only regroups classes and does not resample) (Tables III-VIII).

ICVAE changes the conditional VAE by feeding the class label only to the decoder, with a matching objective, and screens generated attacks by a per-class reconstruction-loss bound (Sec. 3.2, Eq. 4-5, Sec. 4.1-4.2), a stated change of conditioning, so own; compared with ROS, SMOTE and ADASYN (Tables 6-8).

Hybrid IQRBUwOGA chains radial-based undersampling changed to an inverse-quadratic kernel with a standard-deviation stop and a GenSMOTE-style genetic search of SMOTE oversampling rates with a changed selection operator (Sec. 2.3-2.4, Algorithm 1), a search for how much to oversample with stated changes, so own; results show only before vs after balancing (Table 2, Fig. 3).

PCT-GAN adds a factor-structure loss and an inter-item correlation-preservation loss to the generator objective of a conditional WGAN-GP and is called the main methodological contribution (Sec. 3.3.8), a new loss, so own; benchmarked against ROS, SMOTE, BorderlineSMOTE, ADASYN, CTGAN and TVAE (Sec. 3.3, Sec. 4).

A supervised autoencoder learns a class-preserving latent prior for a single generator trained in new three-player games (ADSO, AMO) with a discriminator and a classifier (Sec. III, Eq. 1-11), a new generative model, so own; compared with BAGAN, GAMO, DFBS and data-space oversampling among other baselines (Tables II-III).

DIAO picks which tiles to replicate and augment by a density-driven score with a KL-divergence stopping rule, and DIAO-CP adds Copy-Paste with a background-selection filter for context-aware placement (Algorithms 2-3), a new allocation and placement rule, so own; compared with standard augmentation and stochastic Copy-Paste (Tables 3, 6-8).

Quantum-SMOTEV2 changes the authors' Quantum-SMOTE to rotate minority points about a single data centroid and adds angular-outlier boosting of sparse outlier bins (Sec. 3.3-3.4, Algorithms 5-8), a changed SMOTE-family oversampler, so own; experiments only compare no synthetic data and the method with vs without its own AOL step (Sec. 5-6, Table 3).

AEMLO is a new feature-and-label autoencoder trained with a DCCA joint-embedding loss, a similarity-preserving feature reconstruction and a ranking loss for labels, decoding minority seeds into new multi-label instances (Sec. 3, Eq. 2-8, Algorithm 1), a new architecture and loss, so own; compared with MLSMOTE, MLSOL, MLROS, MLRUS, MLTL and MLBOTE (Table 2).
